en.p: In coordinate space there are two points $\mathrm{A}(a,\,0,\,0)$, $\mathrm{B}(0,\,10\sqrt{2},\,0)$ and a sphere $S:\ x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=100$. Let $C_1$ be the figure formed by all points $\mathrm{P}$ on sphere $S$ with $\angle\mathrm{APO}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, and $C_2$ the figure formed by all points $\mathrm{Q}$ on sphere $S$ with $\angle\mathrm{BQO}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. When $C_1$ and $C_2$ meet at two distinct points $\mathrm{N}_1$, $\mathrm{N}_2$ and $\cos(\angle\mathrm{N}_1\mathrm{O}\mathrm{N}_2)=\dfrac{3}{5}$, what is the value of $a$? (Given that $a>10\sqrt{2}$, and $\mathrm{O}$ is the origin.) [4 points]
